title: Cap. IV Arg. 5: Eph. 1:5–6 — destinavit εἰς υἱοθεσίαν; adoption only of the faithful
pass_a_gloss: Argument 5. Those whom God destined unto adoption through Jesus Christ, and whom he accepted in Christ as the beloved, those are considered as faithful: But all whom God elected to salvation, as Eph. 1:5, 6 witnesses, he destined unto adoption through Christ, and makes them acceptable in Christ as in the beloved: Therefore all whom he elected to salvation he considered as faithful. The Major is proved from this, that there is no adoption into sons except through faith, John 1:12, As many as received him; and Gal. 3:26, For you are all sons of God through faith in Christ.
pass_b_english: Arg. 5. Their syllogism: those destined unto adoption through Jesus Christ and accepted in Christ as the beloved count as faithful; but Eph. 1:5–6 shows that everyone God elects to salvation he so destines unto adoption through Christ and makes acceptable in the beloved; therefore everyone he elects he considered faithful. They prove the Major from John 1:12 and Gal. 3:26 — no adoption into sons except through faith; you are all sons of God through faith in Christ.
source_text: Arg. 5. Quos Deus destinavit εἰς υἱοθεσίαν per Jesum Christum, quosque in Christo tanquam dilecto acceptos, ii considerantur ut fideles: Sed omnes quos Deus elegit ad salutem, teste Eph. i. 5, 6, destinavit εἰς υἱοθεσίαν per Christum, eosque in Christo tanquam in dilecto gratos facit: Ergo omnes quos elegit ad salutem consideravit ut fideles. Major ex eo probatur, quod nulla est adoptio in filios nisi per fidem, Joh. i. 12, Quotquot eum acceperunt; et Gal. iii. 26, Omnes enim filii estis Dei per fidem in Christo.
